source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Promote consistent use of evidence-based measures that reduce central-line bloodstream infection risk","B":"Replace sterile technique whenever the clinician inserting the central line has extensive experience","C":"Eliminate the need to assess daily whether the central venous catheter remains clinically necessary","D":"Permit individual infection-prevention steps to be skipped whenever venous access appears easy"}}
source_row.rationale: CDC central-line prevention recommendations include hand hygiene, maximal sterile barrier precautions for insertion, chlorhexidine-based skin preparation, and appropriate catheter-site practices. A checklist supports reliable implementation but does not replace sterile technique or ongoing review of line necessity.
source_row.source_detail: Summary recommendations: hand hygiene; maximal sterile barrier precautions during CVC insertion; chlorhexidine skin preparation; prompt removal of catheters no longer essential.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Guidelines for the Prevention of Intravascular Catheter-Related Infections
source_row.stem: During central venous catheter insertion, why should the nurse use a standardized insertion checklist that includes hand hygiene, maximal sterile barrier precautions, and appropriate chlorhexidine skin antisepsis?
